body:
## Why

`hkb groom` (a sibling task) needs every open card's blockers. Today `fetchBoard` deliberately does not fetch
them for every card: on a repo where the GraphQL `Issue.blockedBy` field is unavailable it REST-fills blockers
only for the lanes the tick actually needs — todo and blocked. A groom report built on that would report
`no_blockers` for a triage card that has blockers nobody read, which is a **silently wrong answer**, the one
failure mode the values forbid.

## What

- **`fetchBoard(ctx, { blockers: 'all' })`** in `src/tasks.js`: on a repo without the GraphQL field, REST-fill
  blockers for every **open** card, not only todo/blocked. `blockers: true` keeps today's behaviour exactly;
  `'all'` is the only new value. Boards whose repo *has* the GraphQL field pay nothing either way — the blockers
  arrive in the one query the tick already makes.
- **Report the source.** The returned board (or a field the caller can read) says whether blockers came from
  `graphql` or `rest`, and whether they were filled at all, so a caller can distinguish "no blockers" from "not
  looked up". This is what feeds the `unknown_blockers` kind a sibling implements — an empty list on a repo
  where blockers were never filled must never be reported as `no_blockers`.
- **A doctor line.** Next to the existing `GraphQL Issue.blockedBy` check in `src/doctor.js`: when the field is
  absent, say that `hkb groom` will fill blockers with one REST call per open card, so the cost is visible
  before somebody runs it on a large board.

## Done when

- [ ] `fetchBoard(ctx, { blockers: 'all' })` fills blockers for every open card on a repo with no GraphQL
      `blockedBy`, verified against the fake-gh double, and `blockers: true` is byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- [ ] The result says where blockers came from and whether they were filled.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` names the REST-fill cost when the GraphQL field is absent.
- [ ] A repo **with** the GraphQL field makes no extra request for `'all'` — pinned by a test that counts calls.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass. `src/model.js` is not touched by this task.

## Contract

These are the names, signatures and rules a sibling depends on. Do not invent alternatives; a change here
breaks a task you cannot see.

- **The eleven "Amendments from the adversarial pass" at the top of #191 override its body wherever they
  differ.** Read `hkb show 191` first and treat the amendments as the specification. In particular: reuse
  `computeReady`, `agentsOf` and the walk in `src/track.js` — **do not write `detectCycles`**; `no_goal` is
  `info` when the body already has a Done-when heading; `broad_path` exists and is `ask`; `overlap_pair.why` is
  guard-aware.
- `groomBoard(tasks, { now, caps, pairs = 10, statuses })` is exported from `src/model.js` and takes the raw
  `fetchBoard` array and nothing else — a later card puts the same function behind `hkb serve`'s snapshot.
- `GROOM_KINDS` and `GROOM_ACTIONS` are exported from `src/model.js`. Actions are the closed vocabulary
  `promote · specify · link-under · split · supersede · reprioritise · park · archive`, plus `judge` and `none`.
- `fetchBoard(ctx, { blockers: 'all' })` REST-fills blockers for **every open card** on a repo without GraphQL
  `blockedBy`; `blockers: true` keeps today's todo/blocked-only behaviour.
- The `--json` field names in #191 are **frozen**; later kinds are added to `findings`, never renamed.
- The CLI never emits the word "duplicate". `overlap_pair.why` is "will serialize under path_overlap".
- **`src/dispatch.js` is untouched by this whole track** — the promote step still filters `status === 'todo'`.
- Nothing in this track writes to the board. `hkb groom` is a read, like `hkb dispatch --dry-run`.
goal: fetchBoard(ctx,{blockers:'all'}) REST-fills blockers for every open card on a repo without GraphQL blockedBy, reports where they came from so an empty list is never mistaken for no blockers, and doctor names the cost; blockers:true is unchanged and a GraphQL repo makes no extra call
title: fetchBoard blockers all: fill every open card's blockers where GraphQL blockedBy is missing
